sanskrit: avyaktādi viśeṣāntam avidyālakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam nibodhata yathā hīdaṃ guṇair lakṣaṇam ity uta
english: That which begins with the Unmanifest and ends with the particulars is held to bear the mark of ignorance. Learn now how this is characterized by the qualities.

sanskrit: dvyakṣaras tu bhaven mṛtyus tryakṣaraṃ brahma śāśvatam mameti ca bhaven mṛtyur na mameti ca śāśvatam
english: The two-syllabled word is death; the three-syllabled is the eternal Brahman. 'Mine' is death, and 'not mine' is the everlasting.

sanskrit: karma ke cit praśaṃsanti mandabuddhitarā narāḥ ye tu buddhā mahātmāno na praśaṃsanti karma te
english: Some men, the more dull-witted, praise action; but those who are awakened, the great-souled, do not praise action.

sanskrit: karmaṇā jāyate jantur mūrtimān ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ puruṣaṃ sṛjate 'vidyā agrāhyam amṛtāśinam
english: By action a creature is born, embodied and composed of sixteen parts; but ignorance brings forth the Puruṣa, who is ungraspable and feeds on the deathless.

sanskrit: tasmāt karmasu niḥsnehā ye ke cit pāradarśinaḥ vidyāmayo 'yaṃ puruṣo na tu karmamayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Therefore whoever sees to the farther shore is free of attachment to actions; for this Puruṣa is held to be made of knowledge, not made of action.

sanskrit: apūrvam amṛtaṃ nityaṃ ya enam avicāriṇam ya enaṃ vindate ''tmānam agrāhyam amṛtāśinam agrāhyo 'mṛto bhavati ya ebhiḥ kāraṇair dhruvaḥ
english: He who finds this Self—without a prior, deathless, eternal, undivided, ungraspable, feeding on the deathless—he by these means becomes ungraspable, deathless, and steadfast.

sanskrit: apohya sarvasaṃkalpān saṃyamyātmānam ātmani sa tad brahma śubhaṃ vetti yasmād bhūyo na vidyate
english: Casting off all imaginings and restraining the self within the self, he comes to know that auspicious Brahman, beyond which nothing further is found.

sanskrit: prasādenaiva sattvasya prasādaṃ samavāpnuyāt lakṣaṇaṃ hi prasādasya yathā syāt svapnadarśanam
english: By the very serenity of his being he attains serenity; for the mark of that serenity is like the vision seen in a dream.

sanskrit: gatir eṣā tu muktānāṃ ye jñānapariniṣṭhitāḥ pravṛttayaś ca yāḥ sarvāḥ paśyanti pariṇāmajāḥ
english: This is the course of the liberated, of those firmly established in knowledge, who see that all the workings of the world are born of transformation.

sanskrit: eṣā gatir asaktānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ eṣā jñānavatāṃ prāptir etad vṛttam aninditam
english: This is the course of the unattached, this the eternal law; this is the attainment of those who possess knowledge, this the conduct beyond reproach.

sanskrit: samena sarvabhūteṣu niḥspṛheṇa nirāśiṣā śakyā gatir iyaṃ gantuṃ sarvatra samadarśinā
english: By one who is even toward all beings, free of craving and free of desire, looking on all things alike, this course may be traversed everywhere.

sanskrit: etad vaḥ sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā viprarṣisattamāḥ evam ācarata kṣipraṃ tataḥ siddhim avāpsyatha
english: All this I have declared to you, O most excellent of sage-priests. Conduct yourselves thus without delay, and you shall thereby attain perfection.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca ity uktās te tu munayo brahmaṇā guruṇā tathā kṛtavanto mahātmānas tato lokān avāpnuvan
english: The teacher said: Thus addressed by Brahmā their teacher, those great-souled sages did accordingly, and thereby won the higher worlds.

sanskrit: tvam apy etan mahābhāga yathoktaṃ brahmaṇo vacaḥ samyag ācara śuddhātmaṃs tataḥ siddhim avāpsyasi
english: You too, O greatly blessed one, follow rightly this word of Brahmā as it was spoken, O pure-souled one, and thereby you shall attain perfection.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā śiṣyo guruṇā dharmam uttamam cakāra sarvaṃ kaunteya tato mokṣam avāptavān
english: Vāsudeva said: Thus addressed by his teacher, that disciple then performed the whole of this highest law, O son of Kuntī, and thereupon attained release.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyaś ca sa tadā śiṣyaḥ kurukulodvaha tat padaṃ samanuprāpto yatra gatvā na śocati
english: Having done what was to be done, that disciple, O upholder of the Kuru line, reached that state, having attained which one grieves no more.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ko nv asau brāhmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇa kaś ca śiṣyo janārdana śrotavyaṃ cen mayaitad vai tat tvam ācakṣva me vibho
english: Arjuna said: Who indeed was that brāhmaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and who the disciple, O Janārdana? If this is fit for me to hear, then tell it to me, O mighty one.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca ahaṃ gurur mahābāho manaḥ śiṣyaṃ ca viddhi me tvatprītyā guhyam etac ca kathitaṃ me dhanaṃjaya
english: Vāsudeva said: I am the teacher, O mighty-armed one, and know the mind to be my disciple. Out of love for you this secret has been told by me, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: mayi ced asti te prītir nityaṃ kurukulodvaha adhyātmam etac chrutvā tvaṃ samyag ācara suvrata
english: If you bear love toward me always, O upholder of the Kuru line, then having heard this teaching of the inmost Self, conduct yourself rightly, O man of good vows.

sanskrit: tatas tvaṃ samyag ācīrṇe dharme 'smin kurunandana sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā mokṣaṃ prāpsyasi kevalam
english: Then, when this law has been rightly practiced, O delight of the Kurus, your self cleansed of all sin, you shall attain absolute release.

sanskrit: pūrvam apy etad evoktaṃ yuddhakāla upasthite mayā tava mahābāho tasmād atra manaḥ kuru
english: This very thing I told you before as well, when the hour of battle was at hand, O mighty-armed one; therefore fix your mind upon it.

sanskrit: mayā tu bharataśreṣṭha ciradṛṣṭaḥ pitā vibho tam ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi saṃmate tava phalguna
english: But it is long, O best of the Bharatas, since I have seen my father, O lord; I wish to see him, with your consent, O Phalguna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktavacanaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pratyuvāca dhanaṃjayaḥ gacchāvo nagaraṃ kṛṣṇa gajasāhvayam adya vai
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To Kṛṣṇa, who had spoken these words, Dhanaṃjaya replied: Let us two go this very day, Kṛṣṇa, to the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: sametya tatra rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram samanujñāpya durdharṣaṃ svāṃ purīṃ yātum arhasi
english: Having met there with the king, the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, and taken leave of that unassailable one, you may set out for your own city.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bhyacodayat kṛṣṇo yujyatām iti dārukam muhūrtād iva cācaṣṭa yuktam ity eva dārukaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kṛṣṇa urged Dāruka, saying, 'Let the chariot be yoked'; and within a moment Dāruka announced, 'It is yoked.'

sanskrit: tathaiva cānuyātrāṇi codayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ sajjayadhvaṃ prayāsyāmo nagaraṃ gajasāhvayam
english: Likewise the son of Pāṇḍu gave orders for the retinue: 'Make ready; we shall set out for the city named after the elephant.'

sanskrit: ity uktāḥ sainikās te tu sajjībhūtā viśāṃ pate ācakhyuḥ sajjam ity eva pārthāyāmitatejase
english: Thus addressed, those soldiers made themselves ready, O lord of peoples, and announced to Pārtha of boundless splendor, 'All is ready.'

sanskrit: tatas tau ratham āsthāya prayātau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau vikurvāṇau kathāś citrāḥ prīyamāṇau viśāṃ pate
english: Then the two, Kṛṣṇa and the son of Pāṇḍu, mounted the chariot and set forth, exchanging varied and delightful talk, well pleased with each other, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: rathasthaṃ tu mahātejā vāsudevaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ punar evābravīd vākyam idaṃ bharatasattama
english: To Vāsudeva, who stood within the chariot, the mighty Dhanaṃjaya once again spoke these words, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tvatprasādāj jayaḥ prāpto rājñā vṛṣṇikulodvaha nihatāḥ śatravaś cāpi prāptaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam
english: By your grace the king has won victory, O upholder of the Vṛṣṇi line; the foes have been slain, and a kingdom free of thorns has been gained.

sanskrit: nāthavantaś ca bhavatā pāṇḍavā madhusūdana bhavantaṃ plavam āsādya tīrṇāḥ sma kurusāgaram
english: In you the Pāṇḍavas have found their protector, O slayer of Madhu; making you our raft, we have crossed the ocean that was the Kurus.

sanskrit: viśvakarman namas te 'stu viśvātman viśvasaṃbhava yathāhaṃ tvā vijānāmi yathā cāhaṃ bhavanmanāḥ
english: Maker of all, homage be to you; Soul of all, Source of all—even as I know you, even as my mind is fixed on you.

sanskrit: tvattejaḥsaṃbhavo nityaṃ hutāśo madhusūdana ratiḥ krīḍāmayī tubhyaṃ māyā te rodasī vibho
english: From your splendor the fire that devours the offering ever arises, O slayer of Madhu; delight made of play is yours, and the two world-halves are your magic power, O lord.

sanskrit: tvayi sarvam idaṃ viśvaṃ yad idaṃ sthāṇujaṅgamam tvaṃ hi sarvaṃ vikuruṣe bhūtagrāmaṃ sanātanam
english: In you rests all this universe, whatever is fixed or moving; for it is you who fashion the whole eternal host of beings.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca tathā sthāvarajaṅgamam hasitaṃ te 'malā jyotsnā ṛtavaś cendriyānvayāḥ
english: Earth and the middle air, and all that is fixed and moving—your laughter is the spotless moonlight, and the seasons follow upon the senses as your train.

sanskrit: prāṇo vāyuḥ satatagaḥ krodho mṛtyuḥ sanātanaḥ prasāde cāpi padmā śrīr nityaṃ tvayi mahāmate
english: The ever-moving wind is your breath; wrath is the eternal death; and in your favor abides the lotus-seated Śrī, dwelling ever in you, O great-minded one.

sanskrit: ratis tuṣṭir dhṛtiḥ kṣāntis tvayi cedaṃ carācaram tvam eveha yugānteṣu nidhanaṃ procyase 'nagha
english: Delight, contentment, steadfastness, and patience—and this whole world of moving and unmoving things—rest in you; and you alone, O sinless one, are called the dissolution at the ends of the ages.

sanskrit: sudīrgheṇāpi kālena na te śakyā guṇā mayā ātmā ca paramo vaktuṃ namas te nalinekṣaṇa
english: Even in the longest stretch of time your virtues and your supreme Self could not be told by me; homage to you, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: vidito me 'si durdharṣa nāradād devalāt tathā kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāc caiva tathā kurupitāmahāt
english: You are known to me, O unassailable one, from Nārada and from Devala, and from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, and likewise from the grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tvayi sarvaṃ samāsaktaṃ tvam evaiko janeśvaraḥ yac cānugrahasaṃyuktam etad uktaṃ tvayānagha
english: On you all things depend; you alone are the lord of beings; and what has been spoken by you, O sinless one, is joined with grace.

sanskrit: etat sarvam ahaṃ samyag ācariṣye janārdana idaṃ cādbhutam atyarthaṃ kṛtam asmatpriyepsayā
english: All this I shall carry out rightly, O Janārdana; and this exceedingly wondrous deed has been done out of desire for our welfare.

sanskrit: yat pāpo nihataḥ saṃkhye kauravyo dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ tvayā dagdhaṃ hi tat sainyaṃ mayā vijitam āhave
english: For the wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Kaurava, was slain in battle; it was you who consumed that host, while I but won the victory in the fight.

sanskrit: bhavatā tat kṛtaṃ karma yenāvāpto jayo mayā duryodhanasya saṃgrāme tava buddhiparākramaiḥ
english: By you was that deed wrought through which I gained the victory over Duryodhana in the war, by your wisdom and your valor.

sanskrit: karṇasya ca vadhopāyo yathāvat saṃpradarśitaḥ saindhavasya ca pāpasya bhūriśravasa eva ca
english: And duly was the means shown for the slaying of Karṇa, and of the wicked lord of the Sindhus, and of Bhūriśravas as well.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca prīyamāṇena tvayā devakinandana yad uktas tat kariṣyāmi na hi me 'tra vicāraṇā
english: And whatever you, well pleased, have bidden me, O joy of Devakī, that I shall do; in this I have no hesitation at all.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ ca samāsādya dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram codayiṣyāmi dharmajña gamanārthaṃ tavānagha
english: And going to the king, the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, I shall urge him to grant leave for your departure, O knower of dharma, O sinless one.

sanskrit: rucitaṃ hi mamaitat te dvārakāgamanaṃ prabho acirāc caiva dṛṣṭā tvaṃ mātulaṃ madhusūdana baladevaṃ ca durdharṣaṃ tathānyān vṛṣṇipuṃgavān
english: This journey of yours to Dvārakā pleases me well, O lord; and soon, O slayer of Madhu, you will see your uncle, and the unassailable Baladeva, and the other bulls among the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇau tau prāptau vāraṇasāhvayam tathā viviśatuś cobhau saṃprahṛṣṭanarākulam
english: Conversing thus, the two reached the city named after the elephant, and together they entered it, thronged with men full of joy.

sanskrit: tau gatvā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya gṛhaṃ śakragṛhopamam dadṛśāte mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram
english: Going to the house of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, like the dwelling of Śakra, the two beheld, O great king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men.

sanskrit: viduraṃ ca mahābuddhiṃ rājānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiram bhīmasenaṃ ca durdharṣaṃ mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau dhṛtarāṣṭram upāsīnaṃ yuyutsuṃ cāparājitam
english: And Vidura of great wisdom, and King Yudhiṣṭhira, and the unassailable Bhīmasena, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, seated in attendance on Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and the unvanquished Yuyutsu.

sanskrit: gāndhārīṃ ca mahāprājñāṃ pṛthāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ ca bhāminīm subhadrādyāś ca tāḥ sarvā bharatānāṃ striyas tathā dadṛśāte sthitāḥ sarvā gāndhārīṃ parivārya vai
english: And Gāndhārī of great wisdom, and Pṛthā, and the lovely Kṛṣṇā, and Subhadrā and all the rest, all the women of the Bharatas—these they beheld, all standing about, gathered around Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tataḥ sametya rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭram ariṃdamau nivedya nāmadheye sve tasya pādāv agṛhṇatām
english: Then the two subduers of foes, approaching King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, announced their own names and clasped his feet.

sanskrit: gāndhāryāś ca pṛthāyāś ca dharmarājñas tathaiva ca bhīmasya ca mahātmānau tathā pādāv agṛhṇatām
english: And the two great-souled ones clasped likewise the feet of Gāndhārī and of Pṛthā, and of the King of Dharma, and of Bhīma as well.

sanskrit: kṣattāraṃ cāpi saṃpūjya pṛṣṭvā kuśalam avyayam taiḥ sārdhaṃ nṛpatiṃ vṛddhaṃ tatas taṃ paryupāsatām
english: And having honored the steward Vidura and inquired after his unfailing welfare, together with them they then waited upon the aged king.

sanskrit: tato niśi mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ kurūdvahān janārdanaṃ ca medhāvī vyasarjayata vai gṛhān
english: Then at nightfall, O great king, the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra dismissed the upholders of the Kurus, and Janārdana, to their dwellings.

sanskrit: te 'nujñātā nṛpatinā yayuḥ svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam dhanaṃjayagṛhān eva yayau kṛṣṇas tu vīryavān
english: Dismissed by the king, they went each to his own abode; but the valiant Kṛṣṇa went to the very house of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tatrārcito yathānyāyaṃ sarvakāmair upasthitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ suṣvāpa medhāvī dhanaṃjayasahāyavān
english: There honored according to custom, and provided with every comfort, the wise Kṛṣṇa slept, with Dhanaṃjaya for his companion.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyau dharmarājasya bhavanaṃ jagmatuḥ paramārcitau yatrāste sa sahāmātyo dharmarājo mahāmanāḥ
english: When the night had brightened into dawn, the two, having performed the morning rites and being highly honored, went to the palace of the King of Dharma, where the great-minded King of Dharma sat with his counselors.

sanskrit: tatas tau tat praviśyātha dadṛśāte mahābalau dharmarājānam āsīnaṃ devarājam ivāśvinau
english: Then the two mighty ones, entering, beheld the King of Dharma seated, like the two Aśvins beholding the king of the gods.

sanskrit: tau samāsādya rājānaṃ vārṣṇeyakurupuṃgavau niṣīdatur anujñātau prīyamāṇena tena vai
english: Approaching the king, those two bulls among the Vṛṣṇis and the Kurus took their seats, given leave by him who was well pleased with them.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā medhāvī vivakṣū prekṣya tāv ubhau provāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vacanaṃ rājasattamaḥ
english: Then that wise king, best among speakers and most excellent of kings, seeing that the two wished to speak, addressed them with these words.

sanskrit: vivakṣū hi yuvāṃ manye vīrau yadukurūdvahau brūta kartāsmi sarvaṃ vāṃ na cirān mā vicāryatām
english: I think you both wish to speak, O heroes, upholders of the Yadus and the Kurus. Say on; I shall do all that you ask without delay—let there be no hesitation.

sanskrit: ity ukte phalgunas tatra dharmarājānam abravīt vinītavad upāgamya vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: When this was said, Phalguna, skilled in speech, drew near humbly and spoke these words to the King of Dharma.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ciroṣito rājan vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān bhavantaṃ samanujñāpya pitaraṃ draṣṭum icchati
english: Long has the glorious Vāsudeva dwelt here, O king; with your leave he wishes to go and see his father.

sanskrit: sa gacched abhyanujñāto bhavatā yadi manyase ānartanagarīṃ vīras tad anujñātum arhasi
english: Let him go, granted leave by you, if you think it fit; you should give the hero leave to go to the city of the Ānartas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca puṇḍarīkākṣa bhadraṃ te gaccha tvaṃ madhusūdana purīṃ dvāravatīm adya draṣṭuṃ śūrasutaṃ prabhum
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O lotus-eyed one, blessing be upon you; go, O slayer of Madhu, this day to the city of Dvāravatī, to see the lord, the son of Śūra.

sanskrit: rocate me mahābāho gamanaṃ tava keśava mātulaś ciradṛṣṭo me tvayā devī ca devakī
english: Your going pleases me, O mighty-armed Keśava; long is it since you have seen my uncle and the lady Devakī.

sanskrit: mātulaṃ vasudevaṃ tvaṃ baladevaṃ ca mādhava pūjayethā mahāprājña madvākyena yathārhataḥ
english: Honor my uncle Vāsudeva and Baladeva, O Mādhava, O greatly wise one, in my name, as is fitting.

sanskrit: smarethāś cāpi māṃ nityaṃ bhīmaṃ ca balināṃ varam phalgunaṃ nakulaṃ caiva sahadevaṃ ca mādhava
english: And remember me always, O Mādhava, and Bhīma, foremost among the strong, and Phalguna, and Nakula, and Sahadeva.

sanskrit: ānartān avalokya tvaṃ pitaraṃ ca mahābhuja vṛṣṇīṃś ca punar āgaccher hayamedhe mamānagha
english: When you have looked upon the Ānartas, O mighty-armed one, and your father and the Vṛṣṇis, come again, O sinless one, for my horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa gaccha ratnāny ādāya vividhāni vasūni ca yac cāpy anyan manojñaṃ te tad apy ādatsva sātvata
english: Go then, taking jewels and manifold treasures; and whatever else is pleasing to you, take that too, O Sātvata.

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi vasudhā sarvā prasādāt tava mādhava asmān upagatā vīra nihatāś cāpi śatravaḥ
english: For this whole earth, O Mādhava, has come to us by your grace, O hero, and the foes have been slain.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kauravye dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire vāsudevo varaḥ puṃsām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: As the Kaurava, the King of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, spoke thus, Vāsudeva, best of men, uttered these words.

sanskrit: tavaiva ratnāni dhanaṃ ca kevalam; dharā ca kṛtsnā tu mahābhujādya vai yad asti cānyad draviṇaṃ gṛheṣu me; tvam eva tasyeśvara nityam īśvaraḥ
english: The jewels and the wealth are yours alone, and this whole earth as well, O mighty-armed one; and whatever other riches are in my houses, of those too you are the lord, ever the master.

sanskrit: tathety athoktaḥ pratipūjitas tadā; gadāgrajo dharmasutena vīryavān pitṛṣvasām abhyavadad yathāvidhi; saṃpūjitaś cāpy agamat pradakṣiṇam
english: Saying 'So be it,' and thus honored in turn by the son of Dharma, the valiant elder brother of Gada saluted his father's sister according to custom; and being honored, he made his reverent circuit around them.

sanskrit: tayā sa samyak pratinanditas tadā; tathaiva sarvair vidurādibhis tataḥ viniryayau nāgapurād gadāgrajo; rathena divyena caturyujā hariḥ
english: Duly greeted in return by her, and likewise by all, Vidura and the rest, the elder brother of Gada, Hari, then went forth from the city of the elephant on his divine chariot drawn by four horses.

sanskrit: rathaṃ subhadrām adhiropya bhāminīṃ; yudhiṣṭhirasyānumate janārdanaḥ pitṛṣvasāyāś ca tathā mahābhujo; viniryayau paurajanābhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: Setting the lovely Subhadrā upon his chariot, with the leave of Yudhiṣṭhira and of his father's sister as well, the mighty-armed Janārdana went forth, surrounded by the townsfolk.

sanskrit: tam anvagād vānaravaryaketanaḥ; sasātyakir mādravatīsutāv api agādhabuddhir viduraś ca mādhavaṃ; svayaṃ ca bhīmo gajarājavikramaḥ
english: He whose banner bears the foremost of monkeys followed him, together with Sātyaki, and the two sons of Mādravatī, and Vidura of fathomless wisdom followed the Mādhava, and Bhīma himself, with the might of the king of elephants.

sanskrit: nivartayitvā kururāṣṭravardhanāṃs; tataḥ sa sarvān viduraṃ ca vīryavān janārdano dārukam āha satvaraḥ; pracodayāśvān iti sātyakis tadā
english: Having turned back all those increasers of the Kuru realm, and Vidura too, the valiant Janārdana then said in haste to Dāruka, and Sātyaki likewise, 'Urge on the horses.'

sanskrit: tato yayau śatrugaṇapramardanaḥ; śinipravīrānugato janārdanaḥ yathā nihatyārigaṇāñ śatakratur; divaṃ tathānartapurīṃ pratāpavān
english: Then the crusher of throngs of foes, Janārdana, followed by the hero of Śini's line, set forth—even as Śatakratu, having slain the hosts of his enemies, goes to heaven, so the glorious one went to the city of the Ānartas.
